text:
Continuous Integration, or CI, is a development practice where team members frequently merge their code changes into a shared central repository. Instead of waiting until the end of a project, every change automatically triggers a CI pipeline. This pipeline performs automated builds and runs tests to verify that the new code doesn’t break anything.

The main benefit of CI is catching issues early. If a developer introduces a bug, the pipeline fails immediately, alerting the team right away. Fixing a problem at this stage is much cheaper and faster than discovering it weeks later. Thus, CI keeps the software in a stable, working state constantly, promoting smoother collaboration and faster delivery.
